sources.entry: OpenDisplay - Use a spare iPhone or iPad as a second display for your Mac, wired (USB) or over WiFi, with touch input. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/peetzweg/opendisplay) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: OpenDisplay
summary.one_liner: A free, open-source app that turns an iPhone, iPad, or Android device (or a spare Mac) into an extended second display for a Mac, over USB or WiFi.
use_cases: Use an old iPad as a second monitor for a Mac
Extend a Mac desktop onto an iPhone over USB
Add a portrait-mode monitor for chat or logs
Turn an old Mac into a second display
Use an Android tablet as an extra screen for a Mac
summary.what_it_does: OpenDisplay is two apps: a Sender that runs on the Mac (or a Linux desktop) and a Receiver installed on the iPhone, iPad, Android device or a spare Mac. The Mac creates a virtual extended display, captures it, hardware-encodes it with H.264 or HEVC, and streams it over one direct TCP connection via USB (usbmux) or WiFi. The receiving device shows the screen at Retina (HiDPI) resolution and sends touch input back as mouse events, with tap, drag and two-finger scroll. Several devices can be used at once, and the page states up to three screens has been tested. The page says no account, server or telemetry is involved.
notable: Open source under GPL-3.0, with no subscription, dongle or account needed
Works across different Apple IDs, unlike Apple Sidecar
Can use a spare Mac, Android device, or Linux desktop as a sender/receiver in beta
Supports up to three extra screens with touch and portrait rotation
caveats: Android support is in public beta over WiFi only, and the Linux sender and receiver are beta; USB is not supported on Android yet
The Mac app is a direct download rather than on the Mac App Store because it uses the private CGVirtualDisplay API
WiFi transport is unencrypted, per the page's FAQ; Apple Pencil support is on the roadmap rather than available
Mac-receiver keyboard and mouse input is planned, not yet available
